Step-by-Step

How To Use It

Get up and running locally and in GitHub in 4 simple steps.

1

Clone Repository & Install Dependencies

Download the repository ZIP or clone it, then install the fast dependencies inside code/:

📦 Download ZIP Archive
Terminal 
git clone https://github.com/farukhetro/Linkedin-automation.git
cd Linkedin-automation/code
npm install
2

Get LinkedIn OAuth Refresh Token

Set your Client ID and Client Secret in code/.env.local, then run the built-in OAuth helper:

Terminal 
npm run auth

This launches a local callback server, authenticates via your browser, and prints your long-lived Refresh Token directly in your terminal.

3

Customize Your Skills (Blank & Flexible)

The root skills/ folder is completely blank so you can add your own custom skills! Simply drop any skills.txt, profile.json, or markdown file into skills/ and Claude will tailor every post to your unique tone and expertise.

4

Test The Automation Locally

Trigger the end-to-end flow to fetch articles, analyze trends, write a post, and publish to LinkedIn:

Terminal 
npm run start
Cloud Setup

GitHub Actions Automation

Configure repository secrets and let GitHub Actions run your content schedule 24/7.

GitHub Secrets Checklist

Go to your GitHub repository: Settings > Secrets and variables > Actions > New repository secret. Add the following secrets:

Secret Name Description Action
ANTHROPIC_API_KEY Your Claude API Key
TAVILY_API_KEY Your Tavily Search API Key
LINKEDIN_CLIENT_ID LinkedIn Developer App Client ID
LINKEDIN_CLIENT_SECRET LinkedIn Developer App Client Secret
LINKEDIN_REFRESH_TOKEN Refresh Token from npm run auth
LINKEDIN_ORGANIZATION_ID Your Company / Organization Page ID
⏰

5 Daily Scheduled Windows

Configured in .github/workflows/cron.yml for optimal global engagement:

  • 4:50 AM ET (Commuter feed)
  • 12:59 PM ET (Lunch break)
  • 4:45 PM ET (Afternoon wrap-up)
  • 7:45 PM ET (Evening tech discussion)
  • 9:07 PM ET (Late night browsing)
🌐

Automated GitHub Pages

This documentation site deploys automatically via GitHub Actions:

  1. Open your repo Settings on GitHub.
  2. Click Pages in the left sidebar.
  3. Under Source, select GitHub Actions.
  4. Push your code — GitHub Actions builds and deploys .github/pages/ automatically!
